pins.agent_source: crates/briefed-agent with #11310's planner and acceptance (this commit), built on the environment (release)
pins.host: oa-dev-env-1 (GCE c3-standard-22 spot, us-central1-b): agents, worktrees, builds and grading on one machine (AB_HOST=local)
pins.login: the owner's Claude Code subscription token (same token as ~/work/.secrets/claude-code-oauth-token; checked by hash)

outcome: accepted = the change passes its kinds grade (remote/eval.sh for the fix's Rust tests over every touched crate; the fix's own script tests laid over the change; every check its changed files' kinds need, kinds.py) AND the blind judge accepts (score >= 4). A change with nothing checkable here (Kotlin) is judged by the judge alone. Never from the agent's own report.
order: issues in a seeded random order; per issue each rep rotates the arm order from a seeded start
harness_failures: a trial that hits the login's usage limit is discarded and rerun when the login answers; nothing else is rerun or excluded.
issue_selection: six closed issues fixed by one commit, chosen before any trial from git log since 2026-08-20 for kinds the S2 set lacks: docs only (#10065), a shell script with a Python test (#10257), a Python script with tests, a shell gate and docs (#11284), two multi-crate Rust fixes (#11190 gateway+tenancy, #11281 coder-cloud+coder-working-computer+INVARIANTS.md), and Kotlin glue with no checker here (#11283). None is in S2.
question: #11310: with checks per package kind, multi-package briefings and typed acceptance, does the briefed agent (B0) beat bare Claude Code (A) on success, cost per accepted change and time on issues that are not single-crate Rust fixes?

analysis.primary: accepted rate per arm, issue-weighted, with the difference and a 95% issue-level bootstrap CI (10000 resamples, seed 11211); then cost per accepted from known costs and median/p90 time
analysis.note: 6 issues x 2 reps is a small sample: the CI will be wide; reported as measured, no claim beyond it.
